title: Computing Triplet Embeddings
text: number embedding dimensions d hyperparameter must set fitting. dimensions underfit similarity structure; many overfit noise. right approach treat d unknown, fit embeddings several values, choose smallest d whose hold-loss meaningfully higher best. optimizer stochastic, hold-loss varies across runs d. single fit per dimensionality reliable — good run d = 3 might beat bad run d = 4 chance. estimate_dimensionality() addresses fitting multiple independent random restarts d recording best hold-loss restart.

title: Computing Triplet Embeddings
text: Progress messages printed restart completes. function returns named list two elements. $results one row per (dimension, restart): $summary one row per dimension, best_d flag identifying recommended choice:
code: dim_est <- estimate_dimensionality(   triplet_list = icon_triplets,   dims         = 1:8,       # dimensionalities to evaluate   n_restarts   = 10L,       # independent random restarts per d   max_epochs   = 50000L,   seed         = 42L ) head(dim_est$results) #>   d restart      loss epoch #> 1 1       1 0.6022...   ... #> 2 1       2 0.6019...   ... #> ... dim_est$summary #>   d mean_loss  min_loss    sd_loss best_d #> 1 1    0.601     0.601     0.001   FALSE #> 2 2    0.512     0.510     0.003   FALSE #> 3 3    0.448     0.445     0.004    TRUE   # <-- recommended #> 4 4    0.447     0.443     0.005   FALSE #> ...

title: Computing Triplet Embeddings
text: recommendation uses one-standard-error rule: find dimensionality lowest mean hold-loss, compute one standard error mean (.e. sd_loss / sqrt(n_restarts)), flag smallest d whose mean loss falls within margin. favours parsimony — selects simplest model statistically indistinguishable best.

title: Computing Triplet Embeddings
text: simple plot shows mean loss dimension ±1 SD error bars. vertical dashed line marks recommended d. Look elbow: point increasing d longer reduces loss substantially. one-SE rule formalises returning smallest d flat region curve.
code: s <- dim_est$summary  plot(s$d, s$mean_loss,      type = "b", pch = 19,      xlab = "Dimensions (d)",      ylab = "Mean test loss",      main = "Hold-out loss by dimensionality")  arrows(s$d, s$mean_loss - s$sd_loss,        s$d, s$mean_loss + s$sd_loss,        angle = 90, code = 3, length = 0.05, col = "gray50")  abline(v = s$d[s$best_d], lty = 2, col = "steelblue")
